# An actual zero-slack forest fails the weighted centroid-graph bound

There is an actual convex-compatible homothetic family with two integer coordinates, all four canonical parity roots, and exact Minkowski equality on **every** forest edge, whose weighted centroid graph has maximum depth strictly below one quarter of its total weight. In the interval example the exact maximum is `70/301=10/43<1/4`.

The same finite incidence gives such a graph obstruction in every continuous dimension. This closes the proposed weighted centroid-graph theorem for actual zero-slack homothetic forests, not merely its earlier abstract coefficient relaxation.

It does **not** refute OC. Section 6 proves an all-cap continuous-volume lower bound at one of these very centroids that exceeds the OC target by a factor at least `4/3`. The lost contribution is an explicit paired-threshold contribution from equal fibers.

## 1. The exact integer support

Let

    Q=conv{(1,1),(3,-2),(4,3)}.

Equivalently,

    3z1+2z2>=5,       5z1-z2<=17,
    -2z1+3z2<=1.                                     (1)

The integer points of `Q` are exactly

| i | p_i |
|---|---|
| 0 | `(1,1)` |
| 1 | `(2,0)` |
| 2 | `(2,1)` |
| 3 | `(3,-2)` |
| 4 | `(3,-1)` |
| 5 | `(3,0)` |
| 6 | `(3,1)` |
| 7 | `(3,2)` |
| 8 | `(4,3)` |

For example, enumeration of the integer box `[1,4] times [-2,3]` with the three rational inequalities (1) gives precisely this list. All three edges of the triangle are primitive, its area is `13/2`, and the six other listed bases are strictly interior; these are additional checks, not replacements for the exact enumeration.

Define the positive concave roof

    t(z)=min{14,17-z1-2z2}.                           (2)

At the nine bases its values are

    (14,14,13,14,14,14,12,10,7).                     (3)

Its minimum on `Q` is seven, since it is concave and has vertex values `14,14,7`.

For `R>=0` and `d>=1`, use the standard simplex

    K={x in R^d:x_j>=0, sum x_j<=1},

and the actual body

    C_(R,d)={(z,x):z in Q, x_j>=0,
                        sum x_j<=R+14,
                        sum x_j<=R+17-z1-2z2}.        (4)

This is a full-dimensional compact convex polytope. Its actual positive integer fibers are exactly

    K_i=(R+t_i)K,
    |K_i|=(R+t_i)^d/d!,
    g_i=(R+t_i)(1,...,1)/(d+1).                       (5)

If the convention requires a body equal to the convex hull of its mixed source, take `conv union_i({p_i} times K_i)`. It is full-dimensional, contained in (4), and contains each full prescribed integer fiber. Consequently it has exactly the same positive integer fibers and mixed measure; its projection has no further integer bases by (1).

## 2. All canonical forest edges are exact

Since volume is strictly increasing in `t_i`, the volume-maximal parity roots, with the minimum-Euclidean-norm tie convention on the bases, are

    (1,1): root 0,     (0,0): root 1,
    (0,1): root 2,     (1,0): root 5.                 (6)

The only nontrivial ties are root 0 with point 4 and root 5 with point 3. Their squared base norms are respectively `2<10` and `9<13`, so the designated roots are uniquely selected. The other comparisons with these roots are strict or singleton comparisons. Neither increasing `R` nor changing `d` changes the root choices.

The nonroot edges and partners are

    3->4, partner 5;
    4->1, partner 0;
    6->2, partner 0;
    7->6, partner 5;
    8->7, partner 2.                                 (7)

Their midpoint equations hold in the integer bases. The corresponding roof-value identities are

    14+14=2*14,   14+14=2*14,
    12+14=2*13,   10+14=2*12,   7+13=2*10.

Thus every edge satisfies the exact set identity

    K_F(p)=(K_p+K_vc)/2.                             (8)

All paths terminate: `3->4->1`, `6->2`, `7->6->2`, and `8->7->6->2`. There is no unspecified cycle, missing midpoint fiber, or relaxed volume equality.

## 3. Nine explicit graph caps

The centroid graph in (5) is affinely isomorphic to the fixed nine points

    G_i=(p_i,t_i) in R^3.                             (9)

On its affine hull, the height is recovered from the first continuous coordinate by `t=(d+1)x_1-R`. Therefore each graph halfspace below is an actual ambient halfspace after that affine substitution.

For each row, take the closed halfspace `u dot G>=b`:

| Candidate i | Integer normal u | Threshold b | Exact included indices |
|---:|---|---:|---|
| 0 | `(-1,0,0)` | -1 | `{0}` |
| 1 | `(-1,0,1)` | 12 | `{0,1}` |
| 2 | `(-2,1,0)` | -3 | `{0,2}` |
| 3 | `(0,-1,0)` | 2 | `{3}` |
| 4 | `(0,-1,0)` | 1 | `{3,4}` |
| 5 | `(1,1,1)` | 17 | `{5}` |
| 6 | `(3,3,2)` | 36 | `{5,6}` |
| 7 | `(0,0,-1)` | -10 | `{7,8}` |
| 8 | `(0,0,-1)` | -7 | `{8}` |

All listed candidates lie on the respective boundary; the index sets include every boundary point. Every graph point thus has a containing closed halfspace consisting of at most two graph atoms.

Let `a=(R+14)^d`, measuring the atom weights in units `|K|=1/d!`, and set

    T_d(R)=5(R+14)^d+(R+13)^d+(R+12)^d
                         +(R+10)^d+(R+7)^d.          (10)

Every graph atom has weight at most `a`, so the table gives global graph depth at most `2a`. At point 1 there is the exact graph midpoint

    G_1=(G_0+G_4)/2,

and all three atoms `0,1,4` have weight `a`. Every closed containing halfspace contains atom 1 and at least one of the disjoint atoms 0 and 4. Hence its graph mass is at least `2a`. The table's row 1 attains that bound. Consequently the **exact normalized maximum** of the weighted centroid graph is

    D_graph(R,d)=2(R+14)^d/T_d(R).                     (11)

This is a deterministic graph-point maximum, not a continuous centerpoint outside the graph.

## 4. The rational interval counterexample

Take `d=1` and `R=21`. The actual interval lengths are

    (35,35,34,35,35,35,33,31,28),       total M=301.    (12)

The table's actual atomic cap weights are

    (35,70,69,35,70,35,68,59,28).

Thus

    D_graph(21,1)=70/301=10/43<1/4,
    1/4-10/43=3/172.                                (13)

More generally, for intervals (10)--(11) simplify to

    D_graph(R,1)=2(R+14)/(9R+112).

It equals `1/4` at `R=0` and is strictly smaller for every `R>0`. Its limit as `R` tends to infinity is `2/9`.

## 5. Actual graph obstructions in every continuous dimension

For every fixed integer `d>=1`, formula (11) tends to `2/9<1/4` as `R` tends to infinity. An explicit sufficient integer choice is

    R=63d-7.

Then the smallest radius is `63d` and the largest is `63d+7`. The finite binomial estimate

    (1+1/(9d))^d
       <=sum_(k=0)^d (1/9)^k <9/8                  (14)

uses only `binomial(d,k)<=d^k`. Therefore

    2(R+14)^d < (9/4)(R+7)^d <= T_d(R)/4.            (15)

Equations (11) and (15) give an actual homothetic-simplex counterexample to the weighted centroid-graph quarter-mass claim in every continuous dimension. No dimension change, nonintegral base filtering, or missing positive fiber is involved.

## 6. The original continuous source has a uniform compensating bound

The graph obstruction does not discard the actual volume lying on a halfspace's other side of a fiber centroid. In fact the same point

    y=(p_1,g_1)

already satisfies a stronger original-volume bound than OC requires, uniformly in `R,d`.

The three equal fibers with indices `0,1,4` have radius `R+14`, and their bases are an arithmetic progression with middle point `p_1`. Let their common full fiber be `B=(R+14)K`, its volume be `V`, and its centroid be `g`. For a nonvertical ambient cap through `(p_1,g)`, the common continuous normal `u` induces thresholds `0,s,-s` on these three fibers. The ordinary centroid cap contributes at least `Gamma_d V`. The proved paired-tail theorem in `candidate 732b11a769399016`, Section 1, gives

    |B intersect {u dot (x-g)>=s}|
      +|B intersect {u dot (x-g)>=-s}| >=2 Gamma_d V.

Thus, retaining only these three disjoint source fibers,

    mu(H)>=3 Gamma_d V.                              (16)

All other fibers contribute nonnegative mass. The paired-tail inequality includes proper, empty, full, and support-endpoint thresholds. If the continuous normal is zero, a cap through the middle base contains its entire fiber and at least one of the opposite endpoint fibers, contributing at least `2V>=3 Gamma_d V` because `Gamma_d<=1/2`. A cap containing the candidate with positive margin may be translated to its parallel boundary-through-candidate cap, which only decreases its mass. Hence (16) holds for **all** closed ambient containing halfspaces.

Since every one of the nine fibers has volume at most `V`, their original total satisfies `M<=9V`. Therefore

    depth_mu(p_1,g_1)>=3 Gamma_d V/M
                       >=Gamma_d/3>Gamma_d/4.         (17)

For the interval example the three-fiber block is itself centrally symmetric about `(p_1,35/2)`. Its mass is 105, and every through-point cap contains exactly half that block except that a vertical boundary can include additional full-fiber mass. In particular

    depth_mu(p_1,35/2)>=105/(2*301)=15/86>1/8.          (18)

No assertion that (17) or (18) is the exact maximal original mixed depth is made. They are explicit deterministic all-cap lower bounds and suffice to rule out any interpretation of (13) as an OC counterexample.

For a direct illustration of the missed continuous mass, the graph cap in row 1 becomes, for `R=21,d=1`,

    2x-z1>=33.

Although it contains only the two centroids 0 and 1, the captured original fiber lengths are

    (18,35/2,33/2,17,17,17,15,13,19/2),

whose sum is `281/2`, rather than the graph atom mass 70. More generally the mechanism in (16) pays an entire paired-tail budget `2 Gamma_d V`; the simple rule which counts only whichever endpoint centroid is included pays merely `Gamma_d V` for that pair.

## 7. Scope and verification

Sections 1--5 are a standalone exact obstruction to weighted centroid-graph depth under actual convexity and exact zero-forest relations. They need no paired-tail theorem and no OC assumption. Section 6 separately uses the fully proved, independently audited ordinary paired-tail theorem to explain actual continuous-volume compensation. No graph-only theorem is left implicit as a step toward OC.

The standard-library verifier `../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_actual_nine_base_zero_forest_graph_failure.py` checks the exact support, positive roof, canonical root comparisons, every set-equivalent radius identity, all closed cap index sets and weights, the matching midpoint lower certificate, and the displayed interval compensation arithmetic. The general binomial and paired-tail arguments are stated explicitly above; numerical screens are not proof dependencies.
